title: RAW UNREVIEWED: ordered reagents dissolve silver first and gold only after reversal
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. In Sloane73 Q4, a strong water made from vitriol and saltpetre dissolves silver but explicitly not gold in a mixed material; if gold itself is to be dissolved, sal ammoniac is added to corrosive water. Preserve the material-specific negative under the first reagent and the conditional second-stage reversal, not a general dissolution predicate.

source.observed_content: A mixed gold/silver material is placed into strong water of vitriol and saltpetre; silver dissolves and gold does not, thereby separating them. If gold is to be dissolved, sal ammoniac is then added to corrosive water, which dissolves the gold.

design.mechanism: Bind two material participants (silver and gold) to a first reagent and preserve opposite state outcomes: silver becomes dissolved, gold remains undissolved and separable. A conditional next operation changes the reagent composition with sal ammoniac, after which gold dissolves. The nontrivial relation is material-specific selectivity followed by ordered reversal; 'dissolve' cannot be assigned as a static property of the gold or mixture.
design.unit: Complete Sloane73 Q4 passage, including its mixed-material setup, selective first water and optional gold-dissolving condition.
design.observable_consequence: A future whole-unit construction could use this content only if it preserves the initial negative gold outcome, positive silver outcome, separation consequence, and second-stage condition in which reagent change makes gold soluble. A single undirected 'dissolve metals' account or reversed operation order fails. No target availability or fit is claimed.
